newsitem.title: INDIA: Kashmir shops shut in protest over rights abuses.
newsitem.headline: Kashmir shops shut in protest over rights abuses.

text.p: Shops and businesses were closed on Tuesday in Kashmir's biggest city, Srinagar, in a strike to protest against alleged human rights violations by Indian security forces.

"Kashmir will observe a complete shutdown on May 27 to protest against custodial killings, rape of women, destruction of properties and harassment of innocent civilians by Indian security forces," a statement from a union of transporters and traders said.
Srinagar is the capital of Jammu and Kashmir, mainly Hindu India's only Moslem majority province, where troops have been fighting a seven-year-old separatist rebellion.
Indian authorities deny allegations of human rights violations in Kashmir and say they investigate all such charges and punish soldiers who are found guilty.

Indian troops were deployed in Kashmir to contain a rebellion that broke out in 1990. Officials say at least 224 army and paramilitary soldiers have been punished for human rights violations since then.

Police on Monday arrested a soldier accused of involvement in the alleged rape of a girl. In another case, army authorities have sentenced four soldiers to 10 years in prison for raping four women in 1996.

Dozens of guerrilla groups are fighting for the Himalayan region's independence, or merger with neighbouring Pakistan. Police and hospitals say more than 20,000 people have been killed in insurgency-related violence.
During the last five years, the government says it has investigated 2,600 cases of alleged human rights abuses, of which 2,288 were found false.
